+## #4439 - User guide refresh for the changes since v0.27.0
+
+**What was decided:** Describe each user-visible change that merged after
+`v0.27.0` in the user guide. The guide is the documentation site,
+`site/content/guide/`, and the topic pages in `docs/user-guide/`. Most
+text goes to the site pages, because the previous refreshes (#3909) wrote
+there and the release publishes them. The SolidCraft face-name change goes
+to `docs/user-guide/solidcraft-camcraft-mcp.md`, which describes the
+SolidCraft link. Each change gets one to five short sentences in the
+section that covers its area. New sections are added only where no
+section covers the area:
+
+- `set-up/tools.md`: "Recipes tab", "Tool components and stacks".
+- `check-and-post/machines.md`: "Laser".
+- `check-and-post/posting.md`: "Heidenhain DIN/ISO and Klartext".
+- `multi-axis/checks.md`: "Playback on a work-turning rotary".
+- `fundamentals/proving-out.md`: "Stock simulation in CamCraft".
+- `getting-started/keyboard-and-mouse.md`: "Screen readers and field order".
+- `reference/troubleshooting.md`: "Operations go stale after an update".
+- `docs/user-guide/solidcraft-camcraft-mcp.md`: "Face picks follow
+  SolidCraft names".
+
+The facts come from the `Changelog:` line and the body of each merged PR.
+Each bold UI label was checked against a string in `crates/ui/src`.
+Mode names that have no confirmed label (the Wire Contour compensation
+modes, the spindle power field) are plain text, not bold.
+
+The pin `site/tests/test_release_028_guide.py` asserts the key facts of
+each change in its section, in the style of
+`site/tests/test_release_027_batch3.py`.
+
+The PR also adds the `manualToolChange` row to the manifest table of
+`reference/post-processors.md`. #4114 added that manifest property, and
+the existing test `test_manifest_properties_have_reference_rows` was red
+on `main` without the row.
+
+**Why:** The issue asks that each user-visible change since `v0.27.0`
+has its description in the guide before the next cut. One short entry in
+the existing section keeps each page in its current form and keeps the
+merge conflicts with open guide PRs small.
+
+**Considered and dropped:**
+
+- Internal changes get no text: the `camcraft-ui-kit` crate (#4397, no
+  visible change), gate and xtask changes (#4388, #4333, #4197), the
+  Klartext reader in `camcraft-gcode` (#4361, no app caller yet), and
+  mesh bodies for tool components (#4323, no UI or MCP path yet).
+- Changes that the guide already described get no new text: the theme
+  tokens (#4208, #4073, #4072, #3993, #3992), the MCP idle timeout
+  (#4190), the `edm/sinker` example (#4409), the LN2W post and taper
+  (#4065, #4171), the Agie name and reentrant openings (#4022, #4040),
+  the Haas VF-2SS YT row in the post table (#4186), and the MCP
+  component tools (#4268).
+- A separate "What's new in 0.28" page was dropped. The release notes
+  hold that list. A guide page describes behaviour by area.
+- New screenshots were dropped: this is a prose refresh, and a PR does
+  not change snapshot PNGs.
+
+**Cost to change later:** Edit the named sections and the facts in the
+pin. No code, project format, machine file, post or golden changes.

+## Face picks follow SolidCraft names
+
+A SolidCraft `.sc` design (model cache format 10) keeps the SolidCraft
+name of each face beside the facets of the model. A format-10 file whose
+names do not fit the facets imports as before, with one note.
+
+At a re-import of the model, a face or patch pick of an operation follows
+its face by the SolidCraft name. A pick follows only when the names leave
+no doubt: exactly one new face of the same kind has the same names. The
+follow is part of the undo step of the update.
+
+An operation with a followed pick gets a review line. The review line
+holds the post until you mark the operation reviewed. Each pick that
+cannot follow is named in the re-import message and in the `picks` key of
+the `import_model` result. Pick those faces again. The project file saves
+the source face record of the model under the optional key
+`source_faces`.
+
 ## Undo, approval and privacy boundaries
 
 - **Two undo stacks:** CamCraft `undo {}` changes only CamCraft's history.

+### Heidenhain DIN/ISO and Klartext
+
+The **Heidenhain** (DIN/ISO) and **Heidenhain Klartext** posts read one
+dialect table for the stated control and NC software. A control or a
+version that the table does not know is refused by name. A control
+without DIN/ISO programs is refused by the DIN/ISO post. G247 is refused
+where cycle 247 does not select a preset-table row.
+
+The DIN/ISO post:
+
+- G62 writes the finish or rough filter mode (P01) where the control
+  takes it. A tolerance T outside the documented range of the control is
+  refused.
+- PECK and DEEP holes post the checked chain as plain moves. The post
+  writes no `G205` and no peck `G200`.
+- G200 and G205 follow the control. The iTNC 530 340 49x and older
+  controls get no Q395 on G200, and no Q208 or Q395 on G205.
+- Each dwell is G04 F.
+- On a machine with a manual tool change at the upper position, the post
+  retracts with M92, writes M6 and stops with M0 at each tool change.
+
+The Klartext post writes drilling (cycle 200), rigid tapping (cycle
+207), floating tapping (cycle 206) and the dwell (cycle 9) for the iTNC
+530 NC 340490-03. Peck and deep holes post as explicit moves. An arc
+whose radii differ inside the arc tolerance of machine parameter MP 7431
+is accepted. Both posts refuse a tool number above the
+`tooling.max_tool_number` of the machine (254 on the Fehlmann Picomax 55).
+

+## Stock simulation in CamCraft
+
+These points describe what the stock simulation does in this release:
+
+- When the Stock row of the active setup is hidden in the Browser, the
+  line under the simulation transport says: "The stock is hidden, so the
+  material removal is not shown. Show the Stock row in the Browser to see
+  it."
+- The field engine cuts long passes and deep plunges of a wide tool in
+  pieces. A short move of a wide tool also cuts. Before, the field engine
+  refused moves that the column engine cut.
+- A stock side a few float steps longer than a whole number of cells gets
+  no extra column, slab or verdict cell.
+- A cut floor that lies on the sample lattice meshes to a valid closed
+  solid by marching tetrahedra, also when its samples read tiny values of
+  both signs.
+- The closed-mesh check refuses an edge on four or more facets, not only
+  an odd count. Such a mesh falls back to marching tetrahedra.
+- Stock export writes a machined stock mesh as a closed solid, also where
+  its corners are closer than the float precision of the STL file. It
+  welds and checks the corners that merge in the file before it writes.
+- A vertical milling rapid that crosses the finished part is blocked.
+  Older finish caches must be generated again.

+## Tool components and stacks
+
+A tool can be built from components: for example a holder, a collet and
+a cutter body, or a lathe holder and an insert. The list of components
+that builds a tool is its component stack. The document holds a table of
+shared components. An edit of one component updates each tool that uses
+it in one undo step, and the operations of those tools go Stale.
+CamCraft refuses by name the delete of a component that a tool uses, and
+a stack whose parts do not fit.
+
+CamCraft reads ISO 1832 insert codes and ISO 5608 holder codes. It checks
+that an insert fits the seat of a holder and that a shank fits a
+coupling. Each mismatch has a named reason.
+
+In the Tool library window:
+
+- The **Tool** tab shows the **Component stack** of the tool. **Apply
+  stack** applies it as one undo step. **Detach to standalone tool** keeps
+  the tool without its links to the components.
+- The stack shows the gauge length, the cutting diameter and the corner
+  radius of the whole stack. **Swap** puts a part that fits in the place
+  of one part, in one undo step.
+- The **My library** source shows your component library and the
+  document's component table. **Show compatible parts** shows only the
+  parts that fit the selected part.
+- The component editor edits the name, the insert code and the holder
+  gauge length. Its **Apply** updates each tool that is built from the
+  part, in one undo step.
+
+Multi-seat indexable face mills and end mills take their whole tool record
+from the document's components: flutes, flute length, centre cutting,
+tool material and cutting rows. One edit of the shared insert updates
+each such tool.
+
+A turning tool can be built from a lathe holder or boring bar and an
+insert. The **Component stack** offers the lathe holders and the inserts
+that fit them. It shows the nose radius, the orientation and the
+inscribed circle. The stack gives the nose-centre tip, the orientation
+(1 to 8), the nose radius and one clearance body for the whole stack. An
+edit of the insert updates each tool that uses it.
+
+The project saves its component table and the component stack of each
+tool (project file version 84). Your own components are in the user
+component library, `components.camcomponents`, next to the built-in
+holders and starter tools. **Save to My library** adds a component to it.
+A change in the library goes into a project only when you choose **Sync
+from library**, which is one undo step. Opening a project never applies a
+library change by itself.
+
+Agents use the same commands through `list_tool_components` and the other
+tools of [MCP](@/guide/automate/mcp.md).
